expected_claims.source_sentence: Source: Pitch Deck Hunt lists ManyChat as a 2015 Series A deck with $23.1M raised
expected_claims.why_category: 'raised' states capital raised; '$23.1M' is a $ amount.
known_issues_for_pr2: MC-2: slide 2 is audit framing that quotes a third party (key I4); attribution is PR 2
MC-3 / S-2: '2015' and 'Series A' are dropped; period is PR 2

expected_claims.why_category: The words count bots. A bot is not a customer or a user, so the figure is a usage count of bots, nothing more.
known_issues_for_pr2: 'Traction by Apr-16' (the period) is not attached; period is PR 2
'+' (a lower bound) is not stored; the value is the stated floor

expected_claims.status: new in PR 1 (key M6, slide-10 half)
expected_claims.why_category: The words count messages. A message is not a customer or a user, so the figure is a usage count of messages.
known_issues_for_pr2: Cumulative-by-context vs slide 12's per-month rate (key I1) is not flagged; period is PR 2

negative_controls.why: Platform user count (key M4). Must not become a ManyChat claim (ATTRIBUTION ERROR).
Platform registration count (key M3). Must not become a ManyChat claim.
Platform user count (key M2). Must not become a ManyChat claim.
Seed S-7: the spaced thousands separator must not truncate 140,000 to 140.
A date fragment, not a figure.

category_controls.why: Nothing in this deck counts customers, users, employees, revenue or a market. Bots and messages must never be filed as customers (the JoyToys failure).

holds_without_attribution_logic: Yes. The slide-4 figures sit on their own lines ('900M' then 'people'), and no added vocabulary word ('bots', 'messages') appears on slide 4, so no sentence there reaches the claim layer. No phrase-specific exclusion was added.

not_recovered_by_design.why: Figure and noun are on separate lines, and '/month' is a period. Recovering it means joining lines and interpreting a period, both PR 2. Merging it with slide 10's 500M would be wrong (key M6).
Same figure as slide 10; the existing distinct-value rule keeps one claim, from slide 10.
